name: North Lincolnshire

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers privately rented homes in parts of Scunthorpe's Crosby and Park and Town wards, designated on 3 October 2024 and running to March 2030; it went ahead after the High Court dismissed a landlords' legal challenge, with applications open from 6 October 2025 and a registration deadline of 6 January 2026.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: HMOs with five or more people from two or more households need the national mandatory licence.
licensing.fee: Around £955 for a five-year selective licence (council's estimate before the scheme started)

councilTax.text: £2,348.46 average Band D (2026/27), including the adult social care precept, Humberside police, fire and average parish precepts

housing: North Lincolnshire centres on the steel town of Scunthorpe, with the market towns of Brigg, Barton-upon-Humber and Epworth and many rural villages. Much of the private rented stock is early 20th-century terraces in Scunthorpe's Crosby and town centre areas, where selective licensing now applies. The Isle of Axholme and Humber bank villages are low-lying farmland with cottages and bungalows.
checkinTips: Terraces in Crosby and Park: photograph the rear yard, alley gate, gutters and any damp on back walls and in kitchens.
Homes in the Scunthorpe licensing area: photograph the selective licence and check it shows the right address and expiry date.
Low-lying homes on the Isle of Axholme and the Humber bank: note any signs of past flooding on floors and lower walls.
Rural homes off mains gas: photograph the oil tank, its gauge level and the boiler service label.
Homes near the steelworks: record dust on window sills and frames and the condition of external paintwork at the start.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or safety concerns can contact North Lincolnshire Council's private sector housing team, which runs the selective licensing scheme and can inspect homes.
